status: post-result exploratory protocol fixed before exhaustive feature and subgroup scan; feature-family ablations declared before the final rerun
disclosure: The 41/90 win-loss split and the earlier mass, bulge, gas, and outer-slope summaries were already known. This analysis is forensic and hypothesis-generating, not independent confirmation.
question: What distinguishes the SPARC galaxies in which the locked cluster-selected Solar-screened law has lower untouched-outer-point error than independently refit fixed RAR?

outcomes.primary_binary: outer MSE of independently inner-refit screened law is lower than outer MSE of independently inner-refit fixed RAR
secondary: screened versus simple MOND outer MSE
screened versus RAR outer chi-square per point
screened versus RAR catalog-space outer MSE
screened versus RAR at the same screened-law nuisance parameters
at least 10 percent and at least 20 percent outer-MSE improvement

feature_tiers.core_preoutcome: catalog photometry, morphology, HI, measurement quality, distance method, coordinates, independent density/void summaries, component-only geometry, and inner-observed-curve summaries
feature_tiers.extended_environment: all locally available multiscale Cosmicflows void-cage and tidal descriptors
feature_tiers.mechanistic_inner_fit: core and extended features plus inner-fitted nuisances, inner residuals, and tail/force predictions that do not use outer observed velocities
feature_tiers.outer_descriptive_leakage: features derived from observed outer velocities; descriptive only and excluded from primary predictive claims

categorical: chi-square and bias-corrected Cramer V for multilevel variables
univariate_tests.multiplicity: Benjamini-Hochberg FDR reported separately by test family and globally; q<=0.05 is the exploratory flag

feature_family_ablations: intrinsic catalog and inner-curve features without void, sky-position, or reference-code fields
core plus all extended multiscale environment features
all features including the explicitly labeled outer-outcome leakage control

subgroup_scan.one_feature_thresholds: every distinct numeric midpoint leaving at least 15 galaxies in subgroup and complement, plus every eligible categorical/boolean level
subgroup_scan.pairwise_rules: both directions at 25th, 50th, and 75th percentiles for core and mechanistic summary features; conjunctions require at least 12 galaxies in subgroup and complement
subgroup_scan.multiplicity: Benjamini-Hochberg over every scanned one-feature rule and separately over every pairwise conjunction

claim_rules: Outer-observed-velocity features can explain a result descriptively but cannot establish prospective predictability.
A cross-validated AUC near 0.5 means the apparent subgroups do not generalize, even if an in-sample split looks striking.
No individual p-value is interpreted without its FDR q-value and effect size.
High-dimensional environment features are an exploratory family and must replicate in independent galaxies before theory use.
The screened and RAR models fit different standard nuisances; same-nuisance and independent-nuisance outcomes are both required.
No result from this analysis changes the failed universal galaxy-transfer verdict.
known_unavailable_distinctions: resolved warps, lopsidedness, and noncircular-flow maps
vertical disk thickness and vertical stellar kinematics
molecular gas and circumgalactic gas profiles
stellar age, color, metallicity, IMF, and mass-to-light gradients
complete group membership, nearest massive neighbor, and external tidal field below the Cosmicflows resolution
halo shape or independently measured dark-halo mass
galaxy-scale weak or strong lensing for the same objects
